title: Finite projective module evaluation and coevaluation
statement: Let A be a commutative ring and P a finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] A-module. Put P^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P,A). The canonical evaluation map \operatorname{ev}:P^\vee\otimes_A P\to A is given by \phi\otimes x\mapsto\phi(x), and P^\vee is finitely generated projective. The canonical map P\otimes_A P^\vee\to\operatorname{End}_A(P) is an isomorphism; let \operatorname{coev}:A\to P\otimes_A P^\vee send 1 to the tensor corresponding to \operatorname{id}_P. With canonical associators and unitors, (1_P\otimes\operatorname{ev})\circ(\operatorname{coev}\otimes1_P)=1_P and (\operatorname{ev}\otimes1_{P^\vee})\circ(1_{P^\vee}\otimes\operatorname{coev})=1_{P^\vee}.

source.place: Tag 0FNV, Modules, Example modules-example-dual; finite-projective dual module property also Tag 0FNJ, More on Algebra, Lemma lemma-left-dual-module

proof.text: The existing finite-projective dual theorem states that for a finitely generated projective module, the ordinary dual is finitely generated and projective. It also identifies the canonical evaluation map into the double dual, although only the first assertion is needed here.

source.place: Tag 07VI, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, finite-projective termwise dual in the proof; reused as lem-sf-finite-projective-dual

proof.text: Apply the existing finite-projective tensor-Hom equivalence with its module named M specialized to P, its module named P specialized to P, and its module named Q specialized to A. The canonical map then has source P tensor_A Hom_A(P,A) and target Hom_A(P,P tensor_A A). Using the right-unitor identification P tensor_A A with P identifies the target with End_A(P), and the pure-tensor formula is x tensor phi mapped to (y mapped to phi(y) x). Thus the canonical map P tensor_A P^vee to End_A(P) is an isomorphism. The evaluation map P^vee tensor_A P to A is the contraction phi tensor x mapped to phi(x), so it is exactly the stated canonical evaluation.

source.place: Tag 0FNV, Example modules-example-dual; canonical evaluation and identity tensor correspondence

proof.text: Put $c=\Theta^{-1}(\operatorname{id}_P)$, where $\Theta:P\otimes_A P^\vee\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{End}_A(P)$ is the map of Step 2. Define $\operatorname{coev}(a)=ac$; this is an $A$-linear map and sends $1$ to $c$. Every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so choose $c=\sum_{i=1}^r x_i\otimes\phi_i$. The formula for $\Theta$ gives $\sum_i\phi_i(y)x_i=y$ for every $y\in P$. The first triangle composite sends $y$ to precisely this sum, hence equals $1_P$. For $\phi\in P^\vee$, the second triangle composite sends $\phi$ to $\sum_i\phi(x_i)\phi_i$. Evaluating this functional on $y$ gives $\sum_i\phi(x_i)\phi_i(y)=\phi(\sum_i\phi_i(y)x_i)=\phi(y)$ by $A$-linearity and commutativity of $A$, so it equals $\phi$. The canonical associators simply rebracket pure tensors and the unitors turn scalar tensors into scalar multiplication, giving exactly the two asserted composites. Thus this supplies the verification explicitly omitted by Stacks Tag 0FNV. For $P=0$, take the empty sum: both identity maps are zero; for a rank-one free module take $c=1\otimes\operatorname{id}_A$.

lean.statement: theorem finiteProjectiveModuleDualPairing (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (P : Type v) [AddCommGroup P] [Module A P] [Module.Finite A P] [Module.Projective A P] : Module.Finite A (Module.Dual A P) ∧ Module.Projective A (Module.Dual A P) ∧ Function.Bijective (finiteProjectiveTensorEndMap A P) ∧ (TensorProduct.rid A P).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (LinearMap.lTensor P (finiteProjectiveEvaluation A P)) ∘ₗ (TensorProduct.assoc A P (Module.Dual A P) P).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (finiteProjectiveCoevaluation A P).rTensor P ∘ₗ (TensorProduct.lid A P).symm.toLinearMap = (LinearMap.id : P →ₗ[A] P) ∧ (TensorProduct.lid A (Module.Dual A P)).toLinearMap ∘ₗ (finiteProjectiveEvaluation A P).rTensor (Module.Dual A P) ∘ₗ (TensorProduct.assoc A (Module.Dual A P) P (Module.Dual A P)).symm.toLinearMap ∘ₗ (finiteProjectiveCoevaluation A P).lTensor (Module.Dual A P) ∘ₗ (TensorProduct.rid A (Module.Dual A P)).symm.toLinearMap = (LinearMap.id : Module.Dual A P →ₗ[A] Module.Dual A P)
